body:
Stopped before claiming #1862 because its required dependencies #1860 and #1861 are unavailable on an allowed base.
Upstream main 6f8b309dcea9ea2c367ecfa53261ed140881bab3 has no crates/geometry/src/dxf reader or the requested DXF sketch-chaining implementation.
#1860 is open. Its latest comment reports uncommitted work, with no push or PR.
#1861 is open. Its latest comment reports that it stopped because #1860 is unavailable.
The open-PR search found no PR for either prerequisite to stack on.
Implementing those prerequisites here would exceed the instruction to work only #1862.
No claim, worktree, code change, pinning test, or gate run was made for #1862. The per-file overlap check was not started.
The next attempt needs both prerequisites on an allowed base, within the one-level stacking limit.

The maintainer added this to the DXF work in chat on 2026-11-15.

His words: "A DXF should be possible to "place" on a stock and used as references for cutting - not be treated like a model - thus for processes like wireedm, plasma, laser, etc etc.. we can just make a sheet, cube, cylinder. place the DXF - and select operations accordingly. The Adding DXF Profile, should thus live on "Stock page" and have a "virtual" model reference, just so the operations pages gets happy about a model being loaded.."

Change to the scope of this issue:

1. A DXF drawing is a profile that the user places on the stock of a setup. It is not a model.
2. A setup with a stock (a sheet, a block or a cylinder) and no model is a legal setup. The user makes the stock, places the DXF profile on it, and adds operations.
3. The `Sketch` entity belongs to the setup. Its `Location` is relative to the stock: the default is the top face of the stock, at the stock origin. The user can move and rotate it on that face.
4. The command adds the profile to a setup (`ImportDxf` gets the setup as an argument). Undo removes it. The MCP tool and the script verb get the same argument.
5. The setup gets a virtual model reference when it has a placed profile and no model. Each check that asks "is a model loaded" accepts that reference. The reference has no facets, thus 3D solid tools never read it as a mesh.
6. The gouge, collision and verify checks must not pass silently because the model is virtual. Each operation on a sketch states what it checks against (the stock and the sketch chains). An operation that needs a solid model refuses by name on a virtual reference.
7. Record the design of the virtual reference in `docs/decisions/`: what it is in the ECS, what the project file stores, and which checks read it.

Done means, in addition to the list in the issue body:

- A setup with only a stock and a placed DXF profile saves, loads, and accepts a 2D operation on the sketch chains.
- A 3D operation on that setup refuses with a message that names the missing solid model.
- Pins: the placement on the stock top, the move on the stock, undo and redo, and the two refusals.

The UI part of this change is on #1863.
